terms.gloss: traditional, handed down from one’s fathers; native
evidence: Cic. Sen. 37: vigēbat in illā domō mōs patrius et disciplīna
terms.comment: Of one’s fathers, and so of one’s people: a traditional song is carmen patrium; one’s native language, patrius sermō (Cic. Fin. 1.4, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Sen. 46: is sermō, quī mōre majōrum ā summō adhibētur in pōculō
terms.comment: Tradition itself is mōs majōrum, the custom of the ancestors (see practice).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 3.8.4: hoc vērō … trālātīcium est
terms.comment: Of edicts and practices passed on from one holder to the next: traditional, and therefore nothing remarkable.

evidence: Cic. Cael. 34: bona paterna et avīta (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: For what is so old that it is held in reverence (Morgan–Owens).

phrases.latin: metuēbant servī, verēbantur līberī, cārum omnēs habēbant; vigēbat in illā domō mōs patrius et disciplīna
phrases.english: the slaves feared him, the children revered him, all held him dear; in that house the ways of the fathers and the old discipline were strong

phrases.latin: mē vērō et magisteria dēlectant ā majōribus īnstitūta et is sermō, quī mōre majōrum ā summō adhibētur in pōculō
phrases.english: for my part I enjoy the presiding at feasts that our ancestors established, and the talk over the cup that, by ancestral custom, the head of the table begins
next came the Magi, singing their traditional hymn
